Here are the step-by-step solutions to the math word problems:

**[id 190]**
John collects peaches for 3 hours, which is $3 \times 60 = 180$ minutes.
Since he collects 2 peaches per minute, he collects a total of $180 \times 2 = 360$ peaches.

**[id 191]**
Each duck eats 3.5 pounds of insects per week.
A flock of 10 ducks will eat $10 \times 3.5 = 35$ pounds of insects per week.
To find the daily requirement, divide by 7 days: $35 \div 7 = 5$ pounds per day.

**[id 192]**
Tom adds a net of $10 - 2 = 8$ trees per year.
Over 10 years, he adds $8 \times 10 = 80$ trees.
Starting with 50 trees, he has a total of $50 + 80 = 130$ trees.
If 30% of the trees die, $130 \times 0.30 = 39$ trees die.
He is left with $130 - 39 = 91$ trees.

**[id 193]**
Friday: Sue has 18 pink flamingos.
Saturday: 1/3 of the pink flamingos ($18 \div 3 = 6$) are painted white. Now she has 12 pink and 6 white flamingos.
Sunday: 18 more pink flamingos are added. She now has $12 + 18 = 30$ pink flamingos and 6 white flamingos.
The difference is $30 - 6 = 24$.

**[id 194]**
Violeta buys 5 crayons at $2 each, costing her $5 \times \$2 = \$10$.
She had $20, so she will get back $\$20 - \$10 = \$10$.

**[id 195]**
The price of one pen is the price of a pencil plus an eraser: $\$1.20 + \$0.30 = \$1.50$.
The price of 8 pens is $8 \times \$1.50 = \$12.00$.

**[id 196]**
There are 40 restaurants each receiving 2 pounds of carrots, totaling $40 \times 2 = 80$ pounds used.
Out of the 200 pounds, the unused amount is $200 - 80 = 120$ pounds.

**[id 197]**
The number of men and women combined is $8417 + 9092 = 17509$.
The remaining population are children: $23786 - 17509 = 6277$ children.

**[id 198]**
Initial cards: 20
Month 1: She collects 3 times her initial number, which is $3 \times 20 = 60$ cards.
Month 2: She collects 20 fewer than month 1, which is $60 - 20 = 40$ cards.
Month 3: She collects twice the sum of month 1 and 2, which is $2 \times (60 + 40) = 2 \times 100 = 200$ cards.
Total cards now = $20 + 60 + 40 + 200 = 320$.

**[id 199]**
Mark edits an equal number for both publishers, so $1000 \div 2 = 500$ sentences for each.
Publisher A pays 5 cents per sentence.
Publisher B pays twice as much, which is 10 cents per sentence.
Mark earns from Publisher A: $500 \times 5 = 2500$ cents.
Mark earns from Publisher B: $500 \times 10 = 5000$ cents.
Total weekly earnings: $2500 + 5000 = 7500$ cents.
